items.title: feat(fleet): probe-based UDS/TCP transport selection for broker clients (#6218)
items.body: Implements #6218 (from the #5699 design adopted 2026-11-05): fleet clients select UDS vs TCP per broker role by probing, instead of fixed routes. ## What changed - **fleet-config**: new `RoleTransport` + `Config::role_transport_choice(role)` + `probe_socket(path)`. Selection order: the `[] transport` config preference wins ("tcp" = TCP without probing, "socket" = the role's Unix socket); with no preference, probe the role socket — file exists + connect succeeds selects UDS, absent or stale selects TCP. Probe behavior is unit-tested for socket-present, socket-absent, and socket-stale cases, plus the pure preference/probe matrix. - **queue client** (`fleet-queue`, client feature now depends on fleet-config): - `broker_sock()` asks fleet-config instead of hardcoding `~/.cache/laptop-agent/broker.sock` (env > config file > the same compiled-in default; load error falls back to the home-anchored path). - Direct path is route-selected: an explicit `REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL` / broker-url file wins and gains a `unix://` form; otherwise the probe choice for the queue-broker role selects a direct UDS roundtrip when the socket answers. A failed UDS attempt falls back to the session-proxy (TCP) route within the same call. Sandbox consumers are untouched: with no live role socket the client keeps the session-proxy route exactly as before. - **queue-broker `DirectSecrets`**: gains a `unix://` form for `QUEUE_BROKER_SECRETS_URL` (same GET /secret/ exchange over the secrets broker's socket; connect failure falls back to the TCP endpoint in the same resolve), and the default endpoint is probe-selected via fleet-config when no URL is configured. Response handling is shared between the legs. - **`fleet secrets` (laptop-local path)**: new `DirectBrokerSource` in fleet-secrets speaks plain HTTP over the secrets broker's own socket, reading the broker token from its token file. `Resolver::default_chain` prepends it only when the probe selects the socket (laptop); on the sandbox the chain is byte-for-byte the historical shape. `fleet secrets list` uses the direct source on the same condition. ## Tests Laptop, `pkgs/fleet`: - `cargo test -p fleet-config` — 26 passed (3 new: preference/probe matrix, probe live/absent/stale, role dispatch) - `cargo test -p fleet-queue --all-features` — 119 passed (new: configured-URL routing, shared response parsing, DirectSecrets endpoint selection + status mapping, UDS resolve roundtrip) - `cargo test -p fleet-secrets` — all passed (new: direct source resolve + list roundtrips over a temp socket, 404 mapping) - `cargo test -p fleet -p fleet-dispatch` — all suites ok Queue task 14372 (lane code-h, direct execution lane). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(fleet-queue): land the #6448 validation contract statement in the validate.rs module header (#6449)
items.body: Phase 4 of design #6448 (closing inventory, #6449): land the validation contract statement where the next field's author will read it — the `validate.rs` module header. Comment-only change (+41 lines, no behavior change): the #6448 rule (validate every forwarded value — type, range, agreement — at the boundary; reject with a field-named error, never clamp, never warn-and-forward), the bounds table as implemented and enforced at the validator / client / broker, the #8276 dep-clamp exception, and the pointer to #9029 for the four rows where the implemented bounds diverge from the design doc's original table. The full closing inventory — every field `task_from_packet` forwards, every payload field `manual_schema_errors` touches or skips, every `get_i64` flag in `client.rs`, and every broker verb parameter on both backends, each dispositioned with file:line evidence — is recorded on #6449 (comment 6835948908). Required dispositions: (a) list `--not-before` is unvalidated and silently narrows listings on the Turso backend → filed #9027; (b) a direct producer exists (pm-stack/dispatch, direct PostgREST RPC + row PATCH bypassing validator and broker) → filed #9028; (c) `timebox_minutes` — no range verdict warranted (positive-integer error + non-standard warning is the right level; 85/402 corpus packets legitimately use non-standard values; no filed instance of harm); (d) corpus re-check over all 402 saved packets: 401 valid, 1 violation (packet-2392.json, #6446 pr-family identity — a saved packet that today's validator correctly rejects). Verification: `cargo test -p fleet-queue` — 55 lib tests pass; `cargo fmt -p fleet-queue --check` clean. (Build note: the pooled target cache held a stale pre-#6218 fleet-config rmeta that broke the first builds; invalidating that one cached unit fixed it — no source change involved.) items.title: feat(fleet): standing sandbox secrets-broker on loopback/UDS (#10582)
items.body: ## Summary Stage 2 of #10582: the sandbox gains a standing secrets-broker on loopback/UDS, spawn-managed by `fleet init`. Secrets resolve locally; no laptop round trip. ```diff builtin_host("sandbox") -> ["proxy"] builtin_host("sandbox") -> ["proxy", "secrets-broker"] ``` ```text fleet init (sandbox, spawn mode) run_init_proxy # unchanged: probe, spawn, shim sync run_init_secrets_broker # NEW probe_socket(secrets-broker.sock) hit -> "already running; nothing spawned" (strict no-op) miss -> spawn `fleet serve secrets-broker` detached with SECRETS_BROKER_BIND=127.0.0.1:4800 + wait for socket dialable (else error, never silent) secrets_broker::run() - bind = SECRETS_BROKER_BIND or 100.99.113.103:4800 + bind = 127.0.0.1:4800 when FLEET_LOCATION=sandbox (else as before) ``` `DirectBrokerSource` socket probe (existing, #6218) selects the local path automatically. No semantics change: same routes, same auth, same cache discipline. ## Evidence Unit suites, worktree `fleet/sandbox-secrets-broker` @ 38667c8e02: 29 suites, all `ok`, 0 failures (`cargo test`: fleet-config 45, fleet-proxy 109, fleet-secrets 28 passed; builtin-map test now asserts `["proxy", "secrets-broker"]`). Isolated proof (fresh temp HOME + XDG_RUNTIME_DIR + XDG_STATE_HOME, `env -i`, fake `bws` first on PATH returning 2 secrets, no session-broker socket present): - `FLEET_LOCATION=sandbox fleet init` → `proxy started` + `secrets-broker started (...; loopback only)`, exit 0. - Re-run → `proxy already running (proto 1); shims current` + `secrets-broker already running (...); nothing spawned`, exit 0. - `GET /secret/wanted.name` over UDS → `200 {"value":"local-proof-value",...,"source":"cache"}`. - `GET /secret/no.such.name` over UDS → `HTTP 404` in **0.035s** (fast, no retry hang). - Loopback enforcement: broker started with widened `SECRETS_BROKER_BIND=0.0.0.0:14812` + `FLEET_LOCATION=sandbox` logged `listening on 127.0.0.1:4800`; no listener on 14812. - Fake-`bws` call log confirms every backing fetch went through the local fake; cached reads add no fetch calls. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way (revert restores proxy-only sandbox map; broker simply never spawns) **Blast Radius:** sandbox-only Init on the sandbox ensures one extra local role; laptop (`systemd`) path untouched. The broker's bind change is gated on `FLEET_LOCATION=sandbox`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(fleet-queue): dual-bind Unix-socket listeners for queue-broker + secrets-broker (#6216)
items.body: Closes #6216 (implementation follow-up from triage task 11033; design in #5699). ## What queue-broker and secrets-broker were TCP-only (`tiny_http::Server::http`). Each now dual-binds its TCP address **and** a filesystem Unix socket serving the same HTTP surface: - **Transport-agnostic handlers.** Both brokers' request handling is extracted to `handle_request(method, target, token header, body) -> (status, JSON)`. The TCP loops adapt tiny_http requests to it; the new shared `uds_http` module adapts Unix-socket requests to the same functions — routes and auth are identical on both transports by construction. - **`uds_http`** (new, `fleet-queue`): minimal HTTP/1.1 over `UnixListener` with the fleet-proxy `serve.rs` stale-socket discipline (connect-probe, unlink if dead, bind), socket dir `0700`, socket `0600`. A live socket owner or a bind failure degrades to TCP-only with a log line, never to exit — the TCP listener stays the established surface. - **Socket paths from fleet-config**: new `queue_broker_socket()` / `secrets_broker_socket()` helpers; env `QUEUE_BROKER_SOCKET` / `SECRETS_BROKER_SOCKET` beat the defaults (`~/.config/queue-broker/broker.sock`, `~/.config/secrets-broker/broker.sock`). - Auth unchanged: `X-Agent-Token` required on both transports, `/health(z)` exempt. TCP listeners, route surface, and client transports untouched. ## Verification - `cargo test -p fleet-queue --all-features` — 39 pass, including 3 new `uds_http` tests (stale-file bind, live-owner detection, 0600/0700 perms, socket round-trip) and all pre-existing broker tests. - `cargo test -p fleet-config` — 16 pass. - Live smoke of both standalone brokers (fixture token files, loopback binds): identical responses over TCP and UDS for `/healthz`, `/health`, `/secrets`; `401` without token on both transports; a killed broker's stale socket did not block restart (rebound and served); `stat` verified socket `0600` / dir `0700`. Queue: task 11120, lane code-w. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Queue and secrets brokers can now accept requests over Unix sockets as well as TCP. * Default socket locations are provided, with environment variables available to override them. Relative paths resolve under the home directory. * Broker health checks remain available without authentication; other requests require a matching, nonempty token. * If a socket cannot be bound or is already in use, the broker continues serving over TCP.
